In this paper, we present a new dataset DESCGEN for automatically generating entity descriptions from relevant documents and mentions, which provides high quality supervision for a highly abstractive version of this task that targets early description of new entities as they emerge.

Following other summarization tasks, we evaluate the quality of generated descriptions by ROUGE ... which measures the overlap of unigram (R-1), bigram (R-2), and the longest matching sequence of words (R-L).

We present two human assessors with source documents and descriptions generated from different abstractive models and asked them to rate descriptions in terms of nonredundancy, fluency, informativeness and faithfulness.

We present two human assessors with source documents and descriptions generated from different abstractive models and asked them to rate descriptions in terms of nonredundancy (does the description avoid repeating information?), fluency (Is the description wellformed and gramatically correct?), informativeness (does the description capture the salient information about the entity?) and faithfulness (Is the description faithful to the source text?).
